subject: Conditional panels  / Absolute panels closing after buttons..

messages.author: e2ca5093917af03b
messages.subject: Conditional panels  / Absolute panels closing after buttons..
parts:
I am a beginner with JS and ShinyR too,

This is what i want to do.

I have a Analyze button in my app.
I would like to disable it once clicked, and than have the app wait for the calculations to be done.
Once done, I'd like to have the conditional panel with absolute panel in it show on a whole screen (like a second page of the app) with the results
Then I'd like to have Close results button on the "results page", which allows to close the results page and go back to main page.


Any ideas how to go about it  ?
If not, i think i could do this myself, if I only had answers to following questions



Can I reset the button so it is 0 again :) ?
Can I pass JS variables into conditionalpanels conditions (not only the input related variables) in shiny R UI files? and if so ? how to do it ? how to reset or a set given JS variable using shinyJS to a given value ?
How to define JS logical variable and how to then toggle it using shiny JS ?
How to make a conditional panel with absolute panel and with a Button2 on it,  appear after Button1 is clicked on MainPanel, and then, make the conditional panel with absolute panel and with a Button2 disappear after Button2 is pressed ?
Best!
Luke

messages.subject: Re: Conditional panels / Absolute panels closing after buttons..
parts: I can show you how to do this, but first, are you sure you wouldn't rather have two tabs in a tabsetPanel? You can control the active tab from the server using updateTabsetPanel. It might be nice for the user to be able to flip back and forth without having to perform the calculations each time...?
